name: Georgia
tagline: From Brasstown Bald and the Armuchee ridges to Darien's marshes and Tybee Island.
intro: Georgia's byways climb the Blue Ridge around Brasstown Bald and the Armuchee ridges of the northwest, cross Piedmont farm and mill country and the pecan groves of the south, and reach the coast at Darien and Tybee Island. This chapter follows the Georgia Scenic Byways Program of the Georgia Department of Transportation, whose State Transportation Board designates each road on the application of a local sponsor. Seventeen corridors are designated, among them a stretch of Interstate 185 and an eleven-mile extension of the Historic Piedmont route into Warren County.

members.name: Altamaha Historic Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 99 and US 17 carry the byway 17 miles from the Sapelo Island visitors center through the Darien waterfront, past the reconstructed blockhouse of Fort King George and the old rice levees of Hofwyl-Broadfield, under moss-hung live oaks.

members.name: Cohutta-Chattahoochee Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Prater's Mill, an 1855 grist mill in Whitfield County, the byway crosses Murray County pastures and climbs SR 52 past Fort Mountain, where an ancient stone wall runs 855 feet along the summit, to a mountaintop overlook.

members.name: Enduring Farmlands Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Starting at the Old Opera House in Hawkinsville, 65 miles of roads in Pulaski and Wilcox counties run to Pineview, Rochelle and Abbeville past pecan groves, horse pastures and fields of cotton and peanuts in Ocmulgee River country.

members.name: Historic Dixie Highway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The old Dixie Highway runs 62 miles from Albany to Thomasville through Camilla and Pelham among pecan groves and live oaks, by Camilla's 1936 Art Deco courthouse and near Radium Springs, Georgia's largest natural spring.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Historic Effingham-Ebenezer Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Sixty miles of state and county roads wind through Rincon, Springfield and Guyton to Ebenezer, founded by German Lutherans, past the sites of Revolutionary-era taverns, river ferries on the Savannah and a stretch of Sherman's march.

members.name: Historic Piedmont Scenic Byway
members.blurb: State routes 15, 16 and 77 and county roads tie Eatonton to Sparta across 82 miles of Putnam and Hancock farmland and Oconee National Forest, crossing the Oconee and Ogeechee rivers near the ancient Rock Hawk effigy.

members.name: I-185 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Thirty-eight miles of interstate between I-85 and the north edge of Columbus roll through mixed pine woods, with Pine Mountain and F.D. Roosevelt State Park, where Roosevelt picnicked on Dowdell's Knob, close by.
members.note: Shown on the map as Interstate 185.

members.name: Meriwether-Pike Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 55-mile loop from Warm Springs, where Roosevelt built his Little White House, runs through Gay and Molena to Manchester, crossing the Flint River and passing the Red Oak Covered Bridge and the millpond at Jones Mill.

members.name: Millen-Jenkins County Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the old railroad depots of downtown Millen, a 35-mile loop runs out through woodland, pasture and scattered farmhouses, then back across wide farmland, a few miles from the clear springs and Civil War prison site at Magnolia Springs.

members.name: Monticello Crossroads Scenic Byway
members.blurb: State routes 11 and 83 fan out north of Monticello for 29 miles through Jasper County pine woods and pasture, on roads once ridden by Methodist circuit riders and by stagecoaches bound from Augusta toward New Orleans.

members.name: Ocmulgee-Piedmont Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the depot in Gray, SR 11 runs north past Round Oak, then an old trail road turns west through the pines of Piedmont National Wildlife Refuge to the mill village of East Juliette on the Ocmulgee.

members.name: Ridge & Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Fifty-one miles of US 27, state routes 136 and 156 and county roads wind between mountain ridges and farm valleys, with a steep gravel road up to John's Mountain Overlook and The Pocket, a CCC camp until 1942.

members.name: Russell-Brasstown Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 41-mile loop out of Helen circles the headwaters of the Chattahoochee, crossing the Appalachian Trail at Hogpen Gap and taking a spur up toward Brasstown Bald, Georgia's highest mountain.

members.name: South Douglas Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 166 crosses about 19 miles of southern Douglas County from the Carroll line to SR 92, through the crossroads of Fairplay and McWhorter, on long wooded stretches that cross the Dog River reservoir.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: South Fulton Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Cochran Mill Road, Hutcheson Ferry Road and SR 70 make a 29-mile loop through the hills and pastures of south Fulton County, past the mill ruins and old millpond at Cochran Mill Park and the country store at Rico.

members.name: Tybee Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The last 11 miles of US 80 run from Turner's Creek across marsh and tidal water to Tybee Island, on Victory Drive, a World War I memorial highway, passing the turn for Fort Pulaski.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Warren County-Piedmont Scenic Byway Extension
members.blurb: The eastern extension of the Historic Piedmont byway follows SR 16 for 11 miles over rolling farm country from Jewell to Warrenton, on a line that was once part of the Okfuskee Trail.
